findings.title: 1 page(s) have almost no content in the server HTML
findings.what: Found on `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/spa/` (0 words in server HTML).
findings.why: The HTML the server sends is nearly empty, so crawlers that don't run JavaScript (most AI crawlers, and Google's first pass) see a blank page.
findings.fix: Server-render or pre-render page content. Only interactive widgets should depend on client JavaScript.

findings.title: 6 pair(s) of indexable pages share most of their main content
findings.why: Pages that differ only by a swapped name (a city, product or tool) look like doorway or scaled content. Google can filter them out or hold down the whole site.
findings.fix: Give each page its own substance: specific details, local proof, its own intro and FAQs. Merge or noindex pages that can't be made unique.

findings.title: 2 title(s) are shared by more than one page
findings.what: 2 cases, for example `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/tools/ssl-checker/` (SSL Checker - Free Online SSL Certificate Test Tool With Detailed Report | Brand).
findings.why: Duplicate titles make pages compete with each other and look templated.
findings.fix: Make each title unique, usually by including the page's specific subject.

findings.title: 2 hreflang link(s) have no return link
findings.what: 2 cases, for example `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/en/` (es → `https://example-security.com/es/` doesn't link back).
findings.why: Search engines ignore an hreflang pair unless both pages point at each other.
findings.fix: Generate hreflang for every language version from one shared list, so each page lists every version, itself included.

findings.title: No XML sitemap found
findings.why: Without a sitemap, new and deep pages are found slowly.
findings.fix: Generate `/sitemap.xml` from the live content data and reference it in robots.txt.

findings.title: 1 indexable page(s) have no canonical tag
findings.why: Without a canonical, Google picks one itself among parameter, slash and tracking variants.
findings.fix: Add a self-referencing absolute canonical to every indexable page through the shared metadata helper.

findings.title: 1 page(s) have JSON-LD that doesn't parse
findings.what: Found on `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/about/` (Expected property name or '}' in JSON at position 2 (line 1 column 3)).
findings.why: Invalid JSON-LD is ignored completely.
findings.fix: Generate JSON-LD with JSON.stringify from data, escape `<`, and validate templates in the Rich Results Test.

evidence.detail: Expected property name or '}' in JSON at position 2 (line 1 column 3)

findings.title: 1 indexable page(s) block snippets (nosnippet or max-snippet:0)
findings.why: Pages that block snippets can't appear as text snippets or be used in Google's AI Overviews and AI Mode.
findings.fix: Remove nosnippet/max-snippet:0 from pages meant to be found; use data-nosnippet on specific sections instead.

findings.title: 1 page(s) show placeholder, test or broken-encoding text
findings.why: Lorem ipsum, TODO, template tokens or mangled characters on a live page look unfinished to visitors and quality reviewers.
findings.fix: Replace the text with real content and add a build check that fails on these strings.

findings.title: 1 page(s) don't have exactly one H1
findings.why: The H1 states the page's topic. None leaves it unclear; several dilute it.
findings.fix: Give every page one H1 matching its main topic. Logos and card titles are not H1s.

findings.title: 1 page(s) mark up FAQ questions that aren't in the page
findings.what: Found on `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/tools/ssl-checker/` (1 of 1: “What is an invisible question?”).
findings.why: Schema that describes content the page doesn't show breaks Google's guidelines and can bring a manual action.
findings.fix: Build FAQPage from the same array that renders the visible FAQ, or remove it.

findings.title: 1 canonical(s) contain a query string
findings.why: Canonicals built from the request URL leak `?utm_` and other parameters, creating duplicates.
findings.fix: Build canonicals from the clean path, never from the incoming request URL.

findings.title: 1 product page(s) show a different price from their schema
findings.why: Google checks structured data against the visible page; a price mismatch can remove the product's rich results or get the listing disapproved.
findings.fix: Generate the schema price from the same data the page displays.

findings.title: 1 internal link target(s) are broken (4xx/5xx)
findings.why: Every broken link is a dead end for visitors and crawlers and wastes the authority passed through it.
findings.fix: Fix or remove each link. Filter generated links (related, next, breadcrumbs) through the set of live pages.

findings.title: robots.txt blocks 1 AI crawler(s)
findings.why: Blocking an AI search crawler, or a fetcher for pages a person asks about, can keep the site out of that assistant's answers, such as ChatGPT, Claude or Perplexity. Blocking a training crawler keeps the content out of that vendor's AI training only: Google-Extended, for one, doesn't remove a site from AI Overviews or AI Mode.
findings.fix: Confirm this is deliberate. A common middle ground blocks training crawlers and allows search crawlers.

findings.title: 1 page(s) carry ratings or reviews in schema
findings.why: Ratings must come from real reviews that are visible on the page. Invented or unsourced ratings risk a manual action that removes rich results sitewide.
findings.fix: Confirm each rating's source. Keep it only if real reviews are shown on the page; otherwise remove it.

findings.title: 7 page(s) below the home page have no BreadcrumbList
findings.why: Breadcrumb rich results still show in Google and clarify site structure.
findings.fix: Render BreadcrumbList from the same array as the visible breadcrumb.

findings.title: 6 page(s) lack a doctype, a charset or a mobile viewport
findings.why: Without a doctype browsers fall back to quirks mode; without a viewport the page renders as a zoomed-out desktop page on phones, and Google indexes the mobile version.
findings.fix: Start every page with `<!doctype html>`, `<meta charset="utf-8">` and `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">` in the shared layout.

findings.title: 6 indexable page(s) have fewer than 150 words
findings.why: Thin pages rarely rank and can lower the site's overall quality signals.
findings.fix: Add useful, specific content, merge the page into a stronger one, or noindex it until it grows.

findings.title: 5 description(s) are shared by more than one page
findings.what: 5 cases, for example `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/` (A perfectly reasonable description for this test page that runs to about one hun).
findings.why: Duplicate descriptions signal templated pages.
findings.fix: Write a specific description for each page.

findings.title: 3 share image(s) don't load
findings.why: The og:image URL doesn't return an image, so shared links show no picture and Google can't use it as the page's thumbnail.
findings.fix: Point og:image at an absolute URL on the public site that returns the image with status 200. A moved file or the wrong host in the metadata helper is the usual cause.

findings.title: 2 title(s) are longer than 60 characters
findings.what: 2 cases, for example `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/tools/ssl-checker/` (80 chars: SSL Checker - Free Online SSL Certificate Test Tool With Detailed Report | Brand).
findings.why: Long titles get cut off in results, often losing the brand or the key phrase.
findings.fix: Keep titles under about 60 characters, main keyword first.

80 chars: SSL Checker - Free Online SSL Certificate Test Tool With Detailed Report | Brand

findings.title: 1 page(s) have no meta description
findings.why: Google then writes its own snippet, often from navigation text.
findings.fix: Write a unique 120–160 character description per page: what you get and why.

findings.title: 1 page(s) skip heading levels
findings.why: Skipped levels break the outline search engines and screen readers use.
findings.fix: Nest headings in order (H1 → H2 → H3). Style with CSS, not heading levels.

findings.title: 1 page(s) redirect with a meta refresh
findings.why: A meta refresh is a slow, client-side redirect. Search engines may treat it as a redirect or may index the empty page; visitors see a flash first.
findings.fix: Replace it with a server-side 301/308 redirect to the final URL.

findings.title: 1 product page(s) use AggregateOffer for a single offer
findings.why: Merchant listings need an `Offer`. `AggregateOffer` is meant for several sellers, so a shop's own product may not qualify for the shopping features.
findings.fix: Emit an `Offer` with `price`, `priceCurrency` and `availability` for products you sell yourself.

findings.title: 1 hreflang value(s) aren't valid language or region codes
findings.why: Codes search engines can't read are ignored. A common mistake is `en-uk`: the United Kingdom's region code is `gb`.
findings.fix: Use an ISO 639-1 language, optionally followed by an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 region (for example `en-GB`), or `x-default`.

findings.title: The site has no favicon that loads
findings.what: Found on `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/` (no icon link on the home page, and /favicon.ico → 404).
findings.why: Google shows the site's favicon next to its name in search results. Without one that loads, results show a generic globe icon, which looks unfinished next to other sites' logos.
findings.fix: Add `<link rel="icon" href="/favicon.png">` to the home page's `<head>`, pointing at a square PNG or ICO of at least 48 × 48 px that returns 200. Keep its URL stable and don't block it in robots.txt.

evidence.detail: no icon link on the home page, and /favicon.ico → 404

findings.title: 1 pair(s) of language versions share their main text
findings.what: Found on `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/es/` (`http://127.0.0.1:<port>/es/` (es) and `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/en/` (en) share 92% of their main text).
findings.why: The versions are listed as different languages, but one wasn't translated. Google works out a page's language from its visible text, so an untranslated version counts as the original language and can't rank for the other one, and the two compete as duplicates.
findings.fix: Translate the title and main text of each version, or drop the untranslated page from hreflang (and the language menu) until it's translated.

evidence.detail: http://127.0.0.1:<port>/es/ (es) and http://127.0.0.1:<port>/en/ (en) share 92% of their main text

findings.title: 1 schema image(s) don't load
findings.why: Structured data points at these images (an article's image, a logo, a video thumbnail), but the URL answers with an error or a web page instead of an image. Google asks for image URLs it can crawl and index, and recipes, movies and vacation rentals show as rich results only with an image.
findings.fix: Restore the file, or fix the URL in the data the schema is built from. Use the full https:// URL of an image on the public site.

findings.title: 11 indexable page(s) don't allow large image previews
findings.why: Without `max-image-preview:large`, Google shows small thumbnails at most, and pages are less likely to appear with large images in Discover.
findings.fix: Add `max-image-preview:large` to the robots meta of indexable pages through the metadata helper.

findings.title: 7 page(s) have a share image but no twitter:card
findings.why: X shows a large image card only when the page asks for one with twitter:card. Without it, X shows at most a small card with a thumbnail, and only when og:type, og:title and og:description are all set.
findings.fix: Add `<meta name="twitter:card" content="summary_large_image">` next to og:image in the metadata helper. X takes the title, description and image from the Open Graph tags.

findings.title: 7 description(s) barely match their page
findings.what: 7 cases, for example `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/` (“A perfectly reasonable description for this test page that runs to about one hun”: 0 of 9 main words are on the page).
findings.why: Fewer than a quarter of the description's main words are on the page. Google uses a description only when it may describe the page better than the page's own text, so this one is likely replaced in results, and visitors who click expect something else. It's usually a copied template or a description left over from an older page.
findings.fix: Rewrite the description from what the page actually says and offers.

findings.title: 6 page(s) don't declare their share image's size
findings.why: Without og:image:width and og:image:height, Facebook and LinkedIn have to download the image before they can lay out the card, so the first share of a page often shows no image.
findings.fix: Emit `og:image:width` and `og:image:height` next to og:image in the metadata helper.

findings.title: 6 indexable page(s) have no structured data
findings.why: Schema tells search and AI engines what each page is.
findings.fix: Add the schema type the profile assigns to each page type.

findings.title: The site is missing 5 recommended security header(s)
findings.why: Security headers protect visitors and are a trust signal, especially for technical audiences.
findings.fix: Add the missing headers at the server or framework level.

findings.title: 5 description(s) are outside 120–160 characters
findings.why: Short descriptions undersell the page; long ones get cut off.
findings.fix: Aim for 120–160 characters.

findings.title: 4 page(s) lack og:title or og:image
findings.why: Without og:title and og:image, shared links on Slack, LinkedIn and X show a bare URL instead of a card. Where og:description is listed too, the page has no description at all, so each platform guesses its text from the page or shows none.
findings.fix: Emit Open Graph and Twitter tags from the metadata helper, with a default image and per-page images for key pages, and og:description from the page's meta description.

findings.title: robots.txt doesn't reference the sitemap
findings.why: The `Sitemap:` line lets every crawler find it without manual submission.
findings.fix: Add `Sitemap: https://…/sitemap.xml` (absolute URL) to robots.txt.

findings.title: robots.txt has 1 invalid Content-Signal value(s)
findings.why: Content-Signal states how AI systems may use the content (search, ai-input, ai-train), each set to yes or no, and Cloudflare is testing a fourth field, use (immediate, reference or full). Anything else is ignored, so the stated preference doesn't apply.
findings.fix: Use only `search`, `ai-input` and `ai-train`, each `yes` or `no`, and optionally `use=immediate`, `use=reference` or `use=full`, for example `Content-Signal: search=yes, ai-train=no`.

findings.title: llms.txt doesn't follow the llms.txt format
findings.what: Found on `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/llms.txt` (no # heading first, no Markdown links).
findings.why: The format starts with a `# Site name` heading, then a short summary and Markdown lists of links. Tools that read llms.txt expect that structure.
findings.fix: Start with `# Site name`, add a one-line `>` summary, then sections of `- [Page](url): description` links.

evidence.detail: no # heading first, no Markdown links

findings.title: No /.well-known/security.txt
findings.why: security.txt tells researchers how to report vulnerabilities.
findings.fix: Publish one following RFC 9116 with Contact and Expires.

findings.title: 1 page(s) have links without a real destination (href="#", javascript:, or no href)
findings.why: Crawlers only follow real URLs. Click-handler navigation hides pages from search engines.
findings.fix: Use real `<a href>` links for navigation and `<button>` for actions.

findings.title: 1 page(s) use generic link text like “click here” or “read more”
findings.why: Anchor text tells search engines what the target is about.
findings.fix: Use descriptive anchors such as “check your DMARC record”.

findings.title: 1 title(s) are shorter than 20 characters
findings.why: Very short titles waste the most visible spot in results.
findings.fix: Describe the page: what it is and who it's for, in under 60 characters.

findings.title: 1 crawled page(s) are noindex
findings.why: Noindex is right for search, filter, account and result pages, and wrong anywhere you want traffic.
findings.fix: Check each against the project's SEO profile. Keep noindex only on page types meant to stay hidden.

findings.title: 1 page(s) have images without an alt attribute
findings.why: Alt text describes images to screen readers and image search. Decorative images still need `alt=""`.
findings.fix: Add descriptive alt text to meaningful images and empty alt to decorative ones.

findings.title: 1 page(s) have images without width and height
findings.why: Images without dimensions shift the layout as they load (CLS).
findings.fix: Set width and height (or an aspect-ratio box) on every image.

findings.title: 1 page(s) lazy-load their main image
findings.why: If the first image is the largest element, lazy-loading it delays LCP. A lazy-loading script (an image whose real file is in `data-src` behind a placeholder) delays it even more, as the script has to run first. On pages a PageSpeed or Lighthouse lab run loaded, Chrome's own LCP check decides instead: the image it found as the largest element, not the first one.
findings.fix: Load the hero image eagerly with high priority (`priority` / `fetchpriority="high"`). In a lazy-loading plugin (Perfmatters, EWWW, WP Rocket, LiteSpeed), exclude the first images or the hero.

findings.title: 1 page(s) have an og:url that differs from the canonical
findings.why: Shares then point at a different URL from the one search engines rank, splitting share counts and signals.
findings.fix: Build og:url from the same value as the canonical in the metadata helper.

findings.title: 1 page(s) use schema with no rich result (HowTo, SearchAction, SpecialAnnouncement, Occupation)
findings.why: Google ended how-to rich results (2023), the sitelinks search box (2024), special announcement rich results (2025), estimated salary rich results (2025). The markup does no harm but earns nothing.
findings.fix: Remove it, or keep it knowingly. Don't promise these rich results.

findings.title: 1 product page(s) have no shipping details in their schema
findings.what: Found on `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/shop/widget/` (Widget security key: 1 of 1 offer(s)).
findings.why: Shipping costs and delivery times can show in Google's merchant listings; without them the listing is less complete.
findings.fix: Add `shippingDetails` to each Offer, or a site-wide shipping policy (`hasShippingService` on the Organization).

findings.title: 1 product page(s) have no return policy in their schema
findings.what: Found on `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/shop/widget/` (Widget security key: 1 of 1 offer(s)).
findings.why: The return policy can show in merchant listings and helps shoppers choose.
findings.fix: Add `hasMerchantReturnPolicy` to each Offer, or once on the Organization.

findings.title: 1 page(s) with hreflang have no x-default
findings.why: x-default tells search engines which version to show visitors whose language matches none of the listed ones.
findings.fix: Add an x-default entry, usually the main version or a language picker.

findings.title: No page asks the browser to start loading the next page early (speculation rules)
findings.why: Speculation rules let Chrome and Edge start loading a page as soon as a visitor shows they're about to open it (hovering over or pressing a link), so it appears almost at once. A few lines in the shared layout turn this on for the whole site; other browsers ignore them.
findings.fix: Add `<script type="speculationrules">{"prefetch":[{"where":{"href_matches":"/*"},"eagerness":"moderate"}]}</script>` to the shared layout, or send a `Speculation-Rules` header from the server or CDN. Leave out links that change something (log out, add to cart) with a `not` condition.

findings.title: 1 internal link target(s) point at a redirect
findings.what: Found on `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/` (links to `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/about`, which redirects to `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/about/`).
findings.why: Linking to a redirecting URL costs a hop on every click and crawl.
findings.fix: Update the links to the final URL (often a missing or extra trailing slash).

evidence.detail: links to http://127.0.0.1:<port>/about, which redirects to http://127.0.0.1:<port>/about/

findings.title: 1 page(s) send large images at full size to every screen (no srcset)
findings.what: Found on `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/legacy/` (1 image(s) over 1,000 px wide, e.g. /big.png (1200 px)).
findings.why: These images are over 1,000 px wide (from their `width` attribute) with no `srcset`, so phones download the full desktop size. web.dev says that can use 2–4 times the data needed, and it slows the page. 1,000 px is this skill's working level, not a Google threshold.
findings.fix: Give large images a `srcset` with three to five widths and a `sizes` attribute, or use the framework's image component (such as Next.js `<Image>`), which writes them.

evidence.detail: 1 image(s) over 1,000 px wide, e.g. /big.png (1200 px)

findings.title: 1 page(s) leave out a language version their other versions list
findings.why: Each version of a page has to list every version, itself included. These pages lack one the pages they link to list, so search engines may not pair it with them and can show visitors the wrong language.
findings.fix: Build each page's hreflang from one shared list of the page's versions, so they all list the same set.

findings.title: 1 page(s) send their title, description, canonical or robots tag after the <head>
findings.why: These tags came after the page's `<head>` had ended, in the `<body>`. Google asks for the title, meta tags and canonical early in the HTML, because it reads only the first 2 MB of a page, and it accepts a canonical only inside the `<head>`, so one sent in the body works only if the page's JavaScript moves it there. Google does read a robots tag anywhere in the page. Next.js 15.2 and later send metadata late on purpose when it loads slowly ("streamed metadata"): browsers and Googlebot, which runs JavaScript, get it in the body, while the bots on Next.js's own list, such as Bingbot, Applebot and the link previews of X, Slack and Facebook, get it in the head. This crawler (user agent seo-supervisor-crawler) isn't on that list, so it saw what a browser gets.
findings.fix: Put these tags in the `<head>`. In Next.js, make `generateMetadata` fast (cache the data it reads), or list the bots that should get the head version in `htmlLimitedBots` in next.config; `/.*/` turns streaming off. Elsewhere, check the template, component or plugin that writes the tags into the body.
